title: Event-Driven Copy Job Execution with Fabric Activator, Generally Available
summary: Microsoft announces general availability of a direct integration that lets a Fabric Activator rule invoke a Copy job as its action, so data movement can be triggered by a detected event (e.g. a file landing or a table changing) instead of running on a fixed schedule, without needing a pipeline in between.
audience: Data engineers and orchestration/platform architects who currently run Copy jobs or pipelines on fixed schedules and want to replace polling-style schedules with event-driven triggers.
why_it_matters: This closes a specific orchestration gap: previously, triggering a Copy job from a detected event required wrapping it in a pipeline; the direct Activator-to-Copy-job action removes that orchestration layer, which matters for teams managing large numbers of scheduled tables where empty runs and schedule sprawl are a real operational cost.
takeaways: Activator can now invoke a Copy job directly as a rule action, with no intermediate pipeline required, and this is now Generally Available.
The stated motivation is eliminating the inefficiency of fixed-schedule data movement: empty runs when nothing changed, and the latency-vs-cost tradeoff of schedule frequency.
Activator rule conditions that can trigger a Copy job include file-created, table-updated, and metric-threshold events, sourced from things like OneLake or Eventstream.
The setup pattern is: create a Copy job, create an Activator rule with a trigger condition, then set the rule's action to 'Invoke Copy job' targeting that job.

claims.text: Fabric Activator can now directly invoke a Copy job as a rule action, without requiring an intermediate Data Factory pipeline, and this capability is Generally Available.
Copy job is described as Fabric's simplest and most scalable mechanism for moving data across multiple clouds and tenants.
Activator is described as a real-time engine that monitors data and reacts to events, in contrast to Data Factory's traditional fixed-schedule execution model.

Fixed-schedule data movement is characterized as having three recurring costs: computing waste from empty runs when no data changed, a latency-versus-cost tradeoff tied to schedule frequency, and operational overhead from managing many schedules across large table counts.

An Activator rule that invokes a Copy job can be triggered from conditions such as a file being created in a monitored location, a table being updated (e.g. in OneLake), or a metric crossing a defined threshold.

The recommended pattern for event-driven data movement is: define a Copy job (source, destination, full-or-incremental mode, mappings) first, then create an Activator rule whose condition triggers that Copy job as its action, replacing a scheduled trigger with an event trigger.

Once an Activator rule invoking a Copy job is enabled, the rule continuously monitors its defined condition and runs the Copy job automatically only when that condition is met, rather than on every scheduled interval.
